name: Abu Simbel: the temples Ramesses carved into a mountain
note: Orientation: two rock-cut temples c. 1264-1244 BC, 280 km south of Aswan, 40 km from Sudan; propaganda to Nubia (gold, trade route); rediscovered by Burckhardt 1813 (sand to the chins), opened by Belzoni 1817; moved 1964-68; the plan of the visit (facade, hall, sanctuary, then the small temple), light in the morning; the Sun Festival on 22 Oct is five days after this visit.

name: Facade of the Great Temple: the four colossi
commons: Abu Simbel great temple facade colossi
note: Four 20 m seated Ramesses II with the double crown; the second from the left lost its head and torso in an earthquake soon after completion (left as found during the move); family members at the knees (Nefertari, Tuya, Bintanath, Nebettawy, Amun-her-khepeshef...); the niche with falcon-headed Ra-Horakhty holding user and Maat = a rebus of the king's throne name User-Maat-Ra; 22 baboons greeting the sun on the cornice; the Greek mercenary graffiti on the leg (Psamtik II, 593 BC, earliest Greek inscriptions).

name: The Hittite marriage stela and the peace treaty
note: Stela at the south end of the terrace recording the marriage in year 34 to a Hittite princess (renamed Maathorneferure), daughter of Hattusili III, sealing the world's first surviving peace treaty (year 21, after Kadesh); a copy of the treaty hangs at the UN; the Hittite king shown bringing her.

name: The Great Hypostyle Hall: Osiride pillars and the Battle of Kadesh
commons: Abu Simbel hypostyle hall Osiride pillars
note: Eight 10 m Osiride statues of the king (white crown south, double crown north); the ceiling with vultures of Nekhbet; north wall: the Battle of Kadesh (1274 BC) in comic-strip form (camp, spies beaten, the chariot charge, the king alone, the Orontes, counting hands); south wall: Syrian, Libyan and Nubian campaigns; the side storerooms; the second hall with Ramesses and Nefertari before the barque.

name: The sanctuary and the sun alignment (22 Feb and 22 Oct)
commons: Abu Simbel sanctuary four statues Ptah Amun Ramesses Ra
note: 65 m deep; the four seated statues: Ptah (Memphis), Amun-Ra (Thebes), the deified Ramesses, Ra-Horakhty (Heliopolis); twice a year the rising sun travels down the axis and lights three of them while Ptah, god of the underworld, stays in shadow; dates shifted by a day after the 1968 relocation (now 22 Feb/22 Oct, originally 21st, possibly birthday and coronation); the festival crowd on those days.

name: The Small Temple of Hathor and Nefertari
commons: Abu Simbel small temple Nefertari facade
note: Dedicated to Hathor and to Nefertari 'for whom the sun shines'; facade with six 10 m standing colossi, four of the king and two of the queen, the queen the same height as the king (almost unique); Hathor-headed pillars inside; Nefertari crowned by Isis and Hathor; the king smiting before the queen; the cow Hathor emerging from the rock in the sanctuary; compare with Nefertari's tomb QV66 on 21 Oct.

name: The rescue: cutting a mountain into 1,036 blocks
wiki: International Campaign to Save the Monuments of Nubia
note: 1964-68, UNESCO campaign, $40 million (about $300 million today), Swedish VBB engineering; the temples sawn into blocks of up to 30 tons by hand-saws to keep cuts thin, lifted 65 m higher and 200 m back, reassembled inside concrete domes (visible from the back door of the hill); the artificial mountain; the rejected alternatives (lifting on jacks, underwater viewing); the gift temples to Spain (Debod), USA (Dendur), Netherlands (Taffeh), Italy (Ellesyia) in thanks; birth of the World Heritage idea.

name: Lake Nasser and drowned Nubia
note: 500 km reservoir created by the High Dam (1964-70), 1/3 in Sudan; 100,000+ Nubians relocated to Kom Ombo (Egypt) and Khashm el-Girba (Sudan), villages, palm groves and 45 temples lost or moved; crocodiles back in the lake; the Toshka project; the Nubian memory that the Nubian Museum (19 Oct) explains; the drive north along it on the 18th.

name: Why here? Ramesses and the gold of Nubia
note: Nubia (Wawat and Kush) as Egypt's gold mine ('nub' = gold, folk etymology), source of soldiers, ivory, ebony, incense; the Viceroy of Kush; Ramesses' seven Nubian temples (Beit el-Wali, Gerf Hussein, Wadi es-Sebua, Derr, Abu Simbel...) as statements of control; the deified king worshipped alongside the state gods; the temple seen from the river by traders coming north.
